chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one in a state of major impurity (janib) should pour water over his head three times; any less than that would not suffice him.

key_terms.جُنُب: One in a state of major ritual impurity, typically after sexual intercourse or ejaculation
key_terms.يُجْزِئُهُ: It suffices him / fulfills the obligation
key_terms.يُفِيضُ: To pour water abundantly or over

ai.seo_question: How many times must water be poured over the head during ghusl for a person in a state of major impurity?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the minimum legal requirement (minimum al-ikmal) for the validity of ghusl by specifying three pours over the head, a ruling that distinguishes between mere wetting and the complete ritual purification required for major impurity. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is frequently cited to argue against the sufficiency of a single pour, emphasizing the thoroughness of the ritual act as a sign of reverence and completeness in obeying divine command. The emphasis on 'not less than that' underscores the principle that while additional pouring is recommended, the core obligation is strictly defined by this tripartite action.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabi’e Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one with sexual impurity should pour the water upon his head, three times, any less than that would not suffice him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘i ibn ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One, because of sexual relation, must pour water on one’s head three times. Less than this is not sufficient.’”
